name: Sahih al-Bukhari
description: The most authentic book of Hadith after the Quran.

name: Sahih Muslim
description: Renowned for rigorous chain of narration (Isnad) and thematic order.

name: Jami' at-Tirmidhi
compiler: Imam Abu Isa Muhammad at-Tirmidhi (209-279 AH)
description: Famous for grading hadiths (Sahih, Hasan, Da'if) and legal commentaries.

name: Sunan Abi Dawud
description: Focuses primarily on legal traditions and jurisprudence (Ahadith al-Ahkam).

name: Sunan an-Nasa'i (Al-Mujtaba)
description: Highest standard of narration scrutiny among the four Sunan collections.

name: Sunan Ibn Majah
description: Completes the Kutub al-Sittah (The Six Major Books), renowned for rich legal topics.

name: Muwatta Malik
description: Earliest surviving text recording early Medina practices and legal traditions.

name: Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal
description: One of the largest compilations of Hadith arranged by Sahabi narrators.

name: Sunan ad-Darimi
description: Authoritative early hadith work often counted in place of Ibn Majah.

name: Riyad as-Salihin (Meadows of the Righteous)
description: Most widely read collection of hadiths on ethics, manners, and daily worship.

name: Al-Adab al-Mufrad
description: Comprehensive treatise solely dedicated to personal conduct, family relations, and manners.

name: Bulugh al-Maram min Adillat al-Ahkam
description: Standard reference for hadith evidence supporting Islamic Jurisprudence.

name: Mishkat al-Masabih
description: Expanded version of Masabih al-Sunnah, popular in South Asian Madaris.

name: Ash-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyyah
description: Dedicated to describing the physical attributes, character, and daily life of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

name: Forty Hadith of Imam Nawawi
description: Essential collection summarizing the foundational pillars and worldview of Islam.

name: Forty Hadith Qudsi
description: Hadiths where the Prophet narrates revelations directly expressed by Allah.
